methodology_cases.claim: NBS announced an age-group unemployment publication suspension in August 2023. In January 2024 it announced age-group rates excluding students and a new 25–29 age group.
methodology_cases.interpretation: Comparisons across the break need a consistent population definition. A lower rate after the change does not by itself measure an improvement among the same people. NBS attributed the change to refining its labor-force statistics.
methodology_cases.title: The youth unemployment series changed its population definition

methodology_cases.claim: NBS revised the preliminary 2023 GDP estimate using the fifth economic census and a simultaneous change to the valuation of owner-occupied urban housing services.
methodology_cases.interpretation: Separate the census revision from the accounting-method effect when comparing output vintages. This is a documented statistical revision; it is not itself evidence that output was fabricated.
methodology_cases.title: GDP revisions combine census evidence and a housing-services method change

methodology_cases.claim: NBS explains that survey unemployment concerns the labor force and that people neither searching nor available for work are outside that denominator. Its methodology distinguishes unemployment from hours and employment quality.
methodology_cases.interpretation: Read unemployment alongside hours, earnings, participation and working-age population. A stable headline alone cannot settle whether work is becoming more secure or better paid.
methodology_cases.title: Unemployment rates leave job quality and inactive workers outside their headline
